messages:
maya: FYI—we just got a customer escalation from AcroHealth saying their p99 latency jumped from ~320ms to ~1.1s starting ~2:15pm UTC. They included sample request IDs. They said behavior looks correlated with bigger batches after the last runtime push.

jonathan: ugh. which model/route? any change in continuous-batcher defaults in the last deploy?

maya: route: /v1/generate (model:redwood-mini-v1), most traffic small prompts but a subset are long histories. We rolled runtime v3.4.1 at 1:45pm—changelog mentioned "continuous batcher optimizations".

ashok: pinging perf logs now. can you drop sample req_ids?

maya: yup: req_9a2f, req_9a2g, req_9a2h. customer attached traces showing long time_in_batch ~600-800ms occasionally.

lina: I pulled the instance metrics. There's a spike in batch sizes around 2:16–2:28pm to 48–60 tokens per batch (max_batch_size is 64). p95 was ok but p99 increased. looks like a small fraction of requests waited full timeout then executed in big batches.

sre-bot: deploy v3.4.1 reported: continuous-batcher: default timeout_ms changed from 10 -> 25, max_batch_size unchanged.

jonathan: there we go — timeout growth explains increased tail. Larger timeout helps throughput but sacrifices tail latency on low-arrival-rate routes. We should confirm traffic pattern for AcroHealth: are they bursty?

maya: customer says they have a mix—most are short interactive flows, occasional bulk export jobs that enqueue long prompts. That probably inflated the batch window.

emily: quick mitigation options: 1) per-route override to lower timeout_ms for /v1/generate for that org; 2) temporary feature flag rollback to previous batcher defaults; 3) fallback policy to disable continuous batching for routes with >X p99. Thoughts?

jonathan: do 1) asap for the org. we can set per-customer config via Dedicated/route config. Also instrument a canary that reduces timeout to 8ms for this route and monitor p99.

ashok: grabbing the config snippet to apply to prod org config now:

```
route_overrides:
  /v1/generate:
    org: acrohealth
    continuous_batcher:
      timeout_ms: 8
      max_batch_size: 32
```

lina: also recommend adding a short-term alert: if p99 > 600ms for a route and median batch_size < 8, automatically reduce timeout_ms. simple rule but will prevent the timeout-hold pathology.

maya: applied the override at 2:42pm UTC. will wait for metrics.

sre-bot: config push successful to org acrohealth (cfg-7721).

jonathan: thanks. let's check metrics in 5 min.

(5m later)

lina: post-change numbers: p50 ~210ms, p95 ~360ms, p99 down to ~420ms from 1.1s. batch_size distribution shows fewer large batches. looks promising.

maya: customer confirmed improvements. they still saw a couple of 900ms spikes tied to export jobs. suggested we flag export endpoints to use a different route or schedule them off-peak.

emily: long-term followups: - revert the global timeout bump until we complete workload analysis, - add per-route default configs, - add a policy engine to auto-tune timeout based on arrival rate percentiles, - document guidance: "prefer swapping long-batch workloads to a bulk-processing route".

jonathan: agree. i'll open a follow-up ticket for a rollback RFC and per-route config defaults. also add a small repro harness to simulate mixed short+bulk traffic to validate future changes.

maya: created ticket RF-1284 with logs & repro steps + customer contact. tagging @ashok to help with automated alert rule.

ashok: got it — I'll prototype the alert/autotune rule and throw a canary in staging.

billing-bot: note: customer reported potential billing noise due to extra tokens processed in large batches. assigned to billing queue for investigation.

maya: thanks everyone. closing the immediate escalation. we'll follow up on the RFC and autotune work items. :thumbsup:
